$comment: heartbeat-lane-allowlist.json — the blast radius of the PR-free heartbeat lane, as DATA.
Design: docs/research/2026-08-25-pr-free-heartbeat-lane-attestation-instead-of-gate.md
Enforcer: src/Core.TypeScript/hygiene/audit-heartbeat-lane-attestations.ts
THIS FILE IS NOT ENFORCEMENT. GitHub rulesets scope by REF, never by PATH, so no forge-side
mechanism confines a bypass actor to these prefixes (design doc section 2). This registry is
read by the lane BEFORE it pushes (refusal) and by the post-hoc audit AFTER it pushes
(detection). A compromised credential ignores both. What bounds the damage is that the
`Branch Safety` ruleset (16189060: deletion + non_fast_forward) carries ZERO bypass actors, so
the lane can APPEND badly and can never ERASE — and an append is compensatable by revert.
$cutoverComment: Lane commits BEFORE this instant are classified PRE-CUTOVER-LEGACY and never fail the audit —
the same grandfathering audit-agencysignature-main-tip.ts uses, and for the same reason: arming
a check must not retroactively redden history it was never in force for.
The far-future default means the audit is ARMED AND GREEN until the maintainer runs the ruleset
change in design-doc section 6 and moves this field to that date. `--cutover <ISO>` overrides it,
which is how the audit is proven able to fail against real history rather than only synthetics.

$comment: Commit author/committer emails that MARK a commit as lane-produced. Offline heuristic only —
a commit object's author field is attacker-chosen. The authoritative record of who bypassed a
ruleset is the forge's own rule-suites ledger (`--online`), which is why bypass_mode MUST be
`always` and never `exempt`: `exempt` writes no audit entry.
$forgeActorsComment: Used only by `--online`. Any actor recorded BYPASSING a ruleset on main that is NOT listed
here is a finding in its own right, independent of what its commit contains. This is the one
input in the whole audit that the pusher does not author.

subjectPrefixes.$comment: A lane commit's subject must start with one of these. Cosmetic; identity decides.

$comment: Every check name the lane MUST list in `Verification-Checks` for the attestation to count.
A lane that runs fewer cannot pass by naming fewer — the required set lives here, not in the
attestation. Semantics of each: design doc section 4.

knownChecks.$comment: Superset of requiredChecks. A name outside this set is UNKNOWN-CHECK: the lane invented vocabulary the audit cannot evaluate.

$comment: Derived by enumerating the last 40 `[heartbeat-batch-merge]` commits on origin/main
(2026-08-25) and generalising each concrete file to its containing lane prefix.
mode = the change classes permitted for a path:
add-only      new files only; modifying or deleting one is a violation
append-only   modification permitted iff the pre-image is a byte PREFIX of the post-image.
Strictly stronger than `deletions == 0` in a unified diff, which permits
interleaving a rewrite among surviving lines.
mutable       whole-file rewrite permitted (a folded state file). The WEAKEST mode; every
entry here is a place the lane can destroy prior content, so the list is
explicit, short, and deliberately not a glob over a directory.
$mutableComment: The three `mutable` entries are exactly the paths `.gitattributes` gives `merge=theirs` or a
(the RS block buffer), and `data/drift-mtth.json` (the published MTTH roll-up). Every one is a
place the lane may overwrite prior bytes, which is why they are enumerated rather than globbed
and why widening this list is the change most worth reviewing.
$denyComment: Belt-and-braces over the allowlist above, which already excludes these. Listed separately so
that a future widening of `allow` cannot silently swallow an executable surface: a path
matching `deny` is a violation even if some `allow` pattern also matches it.

budget.$comment: Refuse a runaway lane. Bytes are the honest unit; file count catches a fan-out bug the byte cap would not.
